title: Project Browser: discover real projects and interpret their evidence
description: Find registered and unregistered example projects, control search depth, sort actual disk usage and read recorded evidence without launching analysis or deleting files.
objectives: Open Project browser under Help and choose bounded search folders.
Use Depth and Scan to discover projects and sort by real byte counts.
Distinguish missing provenance and declared-output stages from actual run history.
Read details, remove only search roots and use the separate tools for journals and data.
prerequisite: Use completed examples from External Masks and Batch Runner. The recording compares a byte-verified private copy of the two-field measured project with a private copy of one four-channel conversion output, including its hidden checkpoint and two other conversion records. These are different examples, not a before-and-after comparison. All 131 original measured-project files and seven original conversion files remain unchanged. The original artifact paths resolve to the measured copy only inside the recording namespace; provenance is not rewritten. Project Browser has no dedicated download, live image preview, Plot control or AI panel. Scan reads project evidence, not every journal. Sorting, depth and root removal use real controls; no analysis, deletion, external file-manager launch or automatic handoff is performed. Normal SQLite access removes only the private registry's empty WAL and 32768-byte SHM. The original databases and other files remain byte-identical.

scenes.narration: Open Help, then Project browser. This shared screen finds project folders and summarizes what is recorded or present on disk. We use real outputs from External Masks and Batch Runner on private copies. It is an inventory tool, not an image-analysis run.

Add folder selects a place to search. At Depth zero, only that folder itself is checked. Our chosen parent contains a project one level below, so the table is empty. An empty result at this depth does not mean the project or its images are missing.

Set Depth to one and choose Scan. The converted image folder appears: about thirty-two megabytes in seven files. Those are four acquired channel images, a conversion map, a status record and a hidden checkpoint. File counts are not counts of cells or independent experiments.

State says unknown, nothing recorded, because this folder has no artifact registry. Stage says nothing run and Last run says never, even though the conversion genuinely completed. These columns reflect declared workflow outputs and recorded artifacts, not every conversion history. Unknown is not evidence that the data are clean or unprocessed.

Add the measured project as a second search root. Its row shows Measure, about ninety-one megabytes, one hundred twenty-nine files and a registry timestamp. If rescan leaves a selected row's details blank, select another row and return. We demonstrate that workaround without changing the application.

Select the measured project and drag the divider to widen its details. Three artifact records are current here, but roughly eighty-seven megabytes remain unregistered. Current describes the recorded comparison, not complete provenance or scientific validity. The Last run detail explicitly says that its timestamp comes from the registry.

Read Stages before interpreting a completion label. This example reports Mask outputs complete because imported arrays, counts and masks exist; it does not prove that Mask segmentation ran. What could run next lists workflow suggestions, not buttons or validation that every suggested analysis suits these experimental data.

Click the Size header to change sort order. We checked both ascending and descending order against actual byte counts, and row selection still points to the correct project. This screen has no separate stage, age, module-status or stale-result filter controls; use its actual sortable columns and search roots.

With both roots present, Depth zero still finds the directly selected measured project, but not the conversion nested under its parent. Returning to Depth one restores both rows. Depth changes the search scope; it does not remove data or change how much analysis has been completed.

Remove stops searching the selected root; it does not delete that folder. We remove the measured root, then add the unchanged project back. Double-clicking its row in this build emits its selection but stays on Project Browser, so do not expect a project or latest-run window to open automatically.

For actual journal details use Run History, for measurement tables use Database Browser, and for cleanup or archiving use Data Manager. In Python, spacr.projects provides discover, scan and browse. All original files remain unchanged; no new analysis was launched. Follow the relevant workflow lesson before acting on a suggested next step.
